quest.title: Scenes from Life in Meropide: A Raw Deal
quest.description: The line for the mail room is exceptionally long...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x100, Primogem x20, Mora x10000, Credit Coupons x280

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: Can anyone help me? Please! I'm begging you! Help this poor soul!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: Oh, thank goodness! Finally, some kind people! You see, it's my son's birthday tomorrow, and I'd like to send him a letter.

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: But to get a letter sent out of the Fortress of Meropide, you have to queue up here, and I don't have the time for that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why not?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: There was a major safety incident in the production zone, so I have to get there immediately. I was hoping someone could stand in line for me, but...

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know this is what I deserve. But my son is innocent. Why should he have to pay for my crimes too?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: All I want is to send him a letter so he knows his father hasn't forgotten his birthday and loves him very much. But I can't even do that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Poor guy... We'll help him, won't we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: You will? ...I don't have much in the way of money on me right now, but I'll be sure to pay you a fair price for your trouble based on the market average!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...The market average?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: Yes. I've lined up for other people before, so I know the going rate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright, don't sweat it! We're happy to help.

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! You're great people. Oh, I forgot to ask for your names. I'm Decembre, and you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon is Paimon and {M#he}{F#she} is {NICKNAME}. We're adventure buddies!

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: #Well it's good to meet you, Paimon, {NICKNAME}. Here's the letter. Just hand it to Lutz over there. You're lifesavers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't worry! We'll take care of it!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Decembre leaves in a hurry after handing over the letter.\nA long time passes before you and Paimon notice that the short queue hasn't moved an inch. You could be here a while...\nSuddenly, your attention is drawn to a conversation between two people behind you.

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is taking forever. And the air is so stuffy here! I can barely breathe...

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: First time queueing here, huh, kid? Welcome to the infamous slowest queue in the Fortress of Meropide. Surprised you've never heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: Lutz has a tendency to slow things down by embellishing the letters as he types them out. Can't help himself! Then, of course, we have to check through them all over again to make sure we're happy with it, blah blah blah...

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? Gods. I'm going weak at the knees...

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: Haha, hang in there, buddy! If you pass out, you'll only have to start all over again tomorrow. It's happened before, you know. One guy's on his third visit and still hasn't managed to send his letter!

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: Third visit? Geez... Sucks to be him...

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: Haha, you bet it does! It takes a special kind of bad luck to fail three times in a row. He's a legend in the Meropide queueing community. We call him "Unlucky Decembre"!

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: If you're interested, I can tell you more about him.

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'm not really in the mood.

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: Ah c'mon, cheer up! Anyway... It all started the day before yesterday. It was sweltering hot that afternoon...

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: I said I'm not... Ugh, whatever. Carry on.

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: Decembre came to me that afternoon, saying he had to line up to send a letter the following day. He asked me if I could cover his shift as a porter in the Coupon Cafeteria.

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: I was gonna say no, because it sounded like more trouble than it was worth. But he gave me the old puppy eyes, and said how he'd missed his chance the last time because he overslept, and how his son was still waiting for his letter...

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: So I took pity on him, and agreed to help him out. But guess what I saw when I got off work yesterday? I saw him looking for someone else to cover his work, and the excuse was still the same — he needed to send a letter.

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: So I went over and asked him what happened. He said he'd learned from his mistakes, and woke up early in the morning to queue up. But he still didn't manage to send the letter due to unforeseen complications.

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: Don't tell me... he joined the wrong line?

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: No, but that's almost as funny as what actually happened. He skipped breakfast to get in the line early, but by the afternoon he was running on empty and starting to lose it...

dialogues.speaker: Upbeat Man
dialogues.text: He tried to push through, but suddenly everything went black, and there was a loud thud. He was out cold, and by the time he regained consciousness, they were closed for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Exhausted Man
dialogues.text: Hahaha, what a loser! ...Wait, did I...? I don't think I had anything to eat either... Crumbs, now my stomach's starting to growl...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did they say Mr. Decembre? Paimon didn't realize what we'd lined up for... Good thing we always have food with us for emergencies!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Hmm. That didn't seem very nice, but Paimon can't put her finger on why...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Queueing for a long time gets tedious and tiring. You start to forget your purpose here.\nOnly the occasional background noise and chatter serves to remind you that, despite how it feels, time is indeed moving.

response.speaker: Exhausted Man
response.text: I'm feeling lightheaded... Man, I really hope I don't have to do this all over again tomorrow.

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: Eat this. You need something in your stomach. Next time, remember to bring food and water when you go on a long queue.

response.speaker: Exhausted Man
response.text: Thank you. But it's crazy that you're talking about this queue like it's a marathon...

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: Hah. Listen up, maggot! This is the most brutal, god-forsaken slice of hell in the whole Fortress of Meropide. It makes Pankration look like a walk in the park!

response.speaker: Exhausted Man
response.text: But... but it's just—

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: Every queuer worth their salt knows to plan properly before committing to join the line. Some people bring a stool for rest breaks. And some of the more hardcore folks have even been known to camp outside the entrance the night before!

response.speaker: Exhausted Man
response.text: ...But it's just a queue...

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: This is no ordinary queue, rookie. This is war! Everyone is expected to give a hundred and ten percent! Even Unlucky Decembre has multiple contingency plans!

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: Sadly, the best-laid plans are no match for fate. On my way back from the production zone earlier, I saw him leaving the line and heading in the direction of the Coupon Cafeteria.

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: So I asked him, "Hey! Aren't you supposed to be in the queue?" And do you know what his answer was?

response.speaker: Upbeat Man
response.text: He'd gotten so fixated on queueing that he forgot the most important thing of all: He didn't bring his letter with him! So he had to leave and come back.

response.speaker: Exhausted Man
response.text: ...I really have to meet this guy. Sounds like quite a character.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? He forgot his letter!? Man... Decembre's luck really is terrible...

choices.text: Wait, then what did he give us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! He handed it right to us... Paimon is getting pretty confused...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's take a peek at it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, let's see what he wrote... Whoa! What the heck is all this? Paimon doesn't see anything about a birthday or Mr. Decembre anywhere...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's almost our turn, {NICKNAME}! Shall we hand in the letter?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: As your tortuous ordeal approaches the end, you reassure yourself that this has all been worth it.\nBut your questions remain unanswered. A chapter has closed, but the story continues.

choices.text: (I'll have to ask him about it later...)
Didn't he give us his letter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, nothing's more important in life than a full stomach!

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: Hey, it's me! Phew...! I made it, just in time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you so out of breath?

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: I just finished up at the abandoned production zone and ran all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Decembre
dialogues.text: So it's done? The letter's been sent? Great!

response.speaker: Decembre
response.text: Oh? So that's the name she gave herself...

response.speaker: Decembre
response.text: Alright, to tell you the truth, a young woman asked me to send this letter for her. She looked really sick to me, so I agreed, and I didn't even take a single Mora! I'm paying for your compensation out of my own pocket...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!?

choices.text: Looking at the contents of the letter, she does seem very sick indeed.

response.speaker: Decembre
response.text: I guess I must've grabbed the wrong letter on my way out... Fiddlesticks! The birthday letter will never get there in time now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Wait, really? So you finally got your letter posted, but it was the wrong one? Wow. You're really living up to your nickname, Decembre.

response.speaker: Decembre
response.text: Fate is a cruel mistress. *sigh*... I'd love to stay and chat, but I gotta rush home and get the right letter now. I hope there's still time...

response.speaker: Decembre
response.text: Here's your compensation, pleasure queueing business with you... Now to post that blasted letter to my son. See you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, but, but... Ugh, why'd he have to leave? Paimon still has a ton of questions for him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Never mind, at least we got some Coupons, hehe... heh... huh? Is this all!? It's not even one meal's worth!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Noooo! Paimon's so hungry, waaaah!

choices.text: We could take another queueing commission?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Starvation suddenly sounds like a great option.
